title: Alien Dictionary
statement: Aliens use the same letters we do, but in a different alphabet order. You get a list of words that is sorted by that unknown order. Work out a letter order that makes the list sorted, and return it as a string. If no order can work, return an empty string. If several orders work, any is fine. Here you get one fixed answer, as the notes explain.

example.caption: Neighbouring words give rules: t before f, w before e, r before t, e before r. The only order that obeys all four is w e r t f.

output.label: rules, then order w e r t f

idea.sentence: Each pair of neighbouring words gives one rule (first different letters), and a topological sort of those rules is the alphabet.

jargon.plain: An order of nodes where every arrow points forward. It exists only if the arrows have no loop.
How many arrows still point at a node. A node with indegree 0 has nothing that must come before it.
Output a node with indegree 0, delete its arrows, repeat. If nodes remain but none has indegree 0, there is a loop.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of words, e.g. ["wrt","wrf","er","ett","rftt"]

vars.meaning: total number of characters in all words

compare.optimalLabel: Read the words once, sort the rules
compare.unit: steps (rough; trying every order is really U!)

rows.name: Try every order
rows.note: Check each permutation of the letters against the word list.

rows.name: Rules + Kahn's sort
rows.note: One pass over neighbouring words gives the rules. The sort touches each letter and rule once.

fast.takeaway: Only neighbouring words matter, and only their first different letter. That turns a pile of words into a small graph.

stages.title: Collect letters
stages.note: Every letter in every word is a node, including letters that end up with no rule.

stages.title: Rules from neighbours
stages.note: Compare each word with the next. The first different letters give a rule. A longer word before its own prefix means no answer.

stages.title: Find the starters
stages.note: Count the rules pointing at each letter. Letters with none are put in the queue.

stages.title: Output and unlock
stages.note: Take a letter from the queue, output it, remove its rules. Letters whose count reaches 0 join the queue.

stages.title: Check for a loop
stages.note: If every letter was output the order is valid. If some are stuck, the rules form a loop, so return an empty string.

edges.title: Prefix trap
edges.why: The shorter word must come first. There is no letter to compare, so check the lengths yourself or you will accept it.

edges.title: Rules form a loop
edges.why: a before b, b before c, c before a. Nobody can go first, so the queue starts empty and nothing is output.

edges.title: One letter
edges.why: No difference, so no rule. The letter is still output because step 1 added it as a node.

edges.title: Letters with no rule
edges.why: Same prefix, no difference, no rules at all. All three letters start with indegree 0 and come out in first-seen order.

gotchas.text: Only the first different letter of two neighbouring words counts. Later letters say nothing, so never add rules for them.
Many orders can be valid. This solution breaks ties by first-seen letter, so it returns one fixed answer. Keep that tie-break the same in every language so tests can compare strings.
An empty string is falsy, and it is also the 'no answer' value. Compare with === '' explicitly. A valid answer is never empty because every word has at least one letter.
Ranging over a map visits keys in random order. Keep the letters in a slice in first-seen order and loop over that, or the output changes from run to run.
Indexing a string gives bytes, not characters. That is right for lowercase a to z, but would split any multi-byte character.

recap.key: Turn each neighbouring word pair into one rule, then output letters whose rule count is zero.
moves: Add every letter as a node
Add the first-difference rule for each neighbouring pair. Word before its own prefix: return empty
Queue the letters with indegree 0, output and unlock
Fewer letters output than exist means a loop. Return empty
